text:
Aisha Kapoor: Heads-up: new PTQ canary shows a spike in funcall parse errors (~0.35%). digging into the raw stream we see replica streams being merged and producing broken JSON because chunk boundaries cut escape sequences / string literals.
Tom B: sample? this sounds like the classic streaming + kv-cache boundary problem.
Aisha Kapoor: sample extract from two replicas: 
```
[replica-a] ...\\"payload\\": {\\"text\\": \\\"Good eveni
[replica-b] ng\\", \\\"meta\\": {\\"id\\": 42}} ...
```
When concatenated naively it sometimes yields valid text, other times the escaped quote becomes malformed and json.loads fails.
Priya Patel: so timing changes in int8/PTQ shifts where the network splits tokens. we need a solution that avoids changing the API too much.
Jin Park: I have two low-risk options: (A) NDJSON per funcall (1 JSON obj per line) so we can parse incrementally without relying on chunk boundaries, or (B) insert a lightweight boundary token (e.g. `<<RWD-BND>>`) between replica fragments at the arbiter and strip it during reassembly.
Tom B: NDJSON is cleaner but is a contract change. boundary tokens are easier short-term. also add a fallback: if merged text doesn't parse, trigger a non-streaming full-response retry (counts toward retry budget).
Aisha Kapoor: agreed on fallback. we should also deploy a small reassembly helper client-side that tries non-destructive fixes before retrying: check brace balance, complete unterminated string quotes if safe, and detect common escape truncation patterns. always log attempted repairs.
Priya Patel: please make repairs conservative — prefer retry over guessing. add a metric `reassembly_attempted` with outcome labels (fixed|retry|failed). tag with model, quant, canary-id.
Jin Park: also propose fragment TTL: if fragments for one response arrive >150ms apart from different replicas, treat as potential cross-response mixing and prefer retry instead of merge. this reduces false merges.
Tom B: I'll add a dashboard tile showing parse-fail rate by quantization (fp16/ptq/int8) and by merge method (concat/ndjson/boundary).
Aisha Kapoor: runbook for a quick canary:
- Turn on boundary-token mode in ensemble arbiter for 2% traffic (canary 5201240X).
- Ship reassembly lib to runtime callers with conservative repairs + logging.
- Implement non-streaming fallback when reassembly returns None.
- Emit `fragment_boundary_mismatch` + `reassembly_attempted` telemetry, with model+quant tags.
deploy-bot: boundary-token canary live on eng-ml staging (5201240030) at 2% :rocket: 
Priya Patel: I'll add an eval comparing pre/post parse error rate on a held-out prompt set, and a small A/B to measure user-visible functional regressions.
Jin Park: if boundary-token reduces errors but causes downstream parsers to choke (edge cases), we'll flip to NDJSON in a followup canary.
Tom B: noted. I'll instrument latency impact of fallback retries too.
Aisha Kapoor: thanks team — please drop a quick post in this thread with the first-hour telemetry snapshot.
